title: Polynomial-time computability of marker removal
statement: For a bit string $z$, take the second component of the total first projection of $z$, then apply the total second projection to that result; failed pair parses yield the empty word. Finally, process the resulting word from left to right, initially outside a marked region: a zero switches the process into the marked region and emits nothing, a one outside the marked region emits nothing, and every bit inside the marked region is emitted unchanged. The function so defined is polynomial-time computable.
